title: the night the soi went dark

opening.dialogue: The blackout takes the soi at nine, and a life is a sending — every phone on the strip migrates toward the one inverter still breathing at Saduek Sak 24.
Bank rolls his bike to the wat steps with his phone already at four percent. 'Six sockets,' he says. 'I counted them before I counted my orders.'
He lifts the orange queue vest off his handlebars and drapes it over the temple rail like a flag that has nowhere to go. 'The funeral stream goes out at ten. The family is three time zones away.'

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He tilts his phone toward Lek, the screen a weak square of light on the temple wall, and taps the charging cable against the biscuit tin.
turns.dialogue: If the inverter holds, I could ride out to the coast after the stream. Sleep on the sand. Save a night's rent. You ever do that?

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He checks the time on the dead phone, then on the wat clock, then on Lek's face, and sets the laundry basket down between them.
turns.dialogue: You're out late for a clerk. The shop closed hours ago. What's in the tin that couldn't wait till morning?

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He crouches and peers into the biscuit tin as if it were a room, one hand flat on the lid to keep the wind from taking the papers.
turns.dialogue: Three vendors' books in a biscuit tin. What's in there that the soi needs tonight more than a charged phone?

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He holds up one palm, the other still on the tin, and shakes his head slowly at the noise from the charging corner.
turns.dialogue: Wait. I'm not finished. The stream needs a phone at full, not five phones at half. That's the whole arithmetic of tonight.

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He taps the temple step twice with two fingers, then points at the inverter cable snaking toward the laundry basket.
turns.dialogue: One phone, one socket, one hour each. That's the best way. The rest of them can queue by the wat bell.

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He looks away at the dark soi, his thumb rubbing the worn corner of the orange vest, and sets it down on the laundry basket.
turns.dialogue: I used to think the night belonged to the riders. Now I look at a dead phone and I don't feel the same about the hours.

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He holds out his pinky over the biscuit tin, the nail split from a dropped order, and waits.
turns.dialogue: Promise me the funeral phone gets the first hour. Not the win chief's radio, not the condo clerk's call. The stream.

turns.speaker: char_bank
stage_directions: He smiles at the stamp-drawer keys in Lek's hand and nods toward the wat door where the novice is waiting with a tripod.
turns.dialogue: You're a good person, clerk. You read for people who can't read and you don't charge the ones who can't pay. That's rare on this soi.

bank_turn_1.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_1.line: He says it lightly, but his thumb is already checking the charge again. The beach is a place he has never been and prices in his head like a fare.

bank_turn_2.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_2.line: He sets the basket down and waits. The soi's dark has made everyone a little more honest about what they carry.

bank_turn_3.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_3.line: He sees the ledgers and the notebook and does not ask to read them. He asks what they are for.

bank_turn_4.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_4.line: He lays out the arithmetic on the step with a piece of chalk from his pocket: six sockets, nine phones, one night.

bank_turn_5.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_5.line: He taps the step again. The queue by the wat bell is already forming in his head, and he is already assigning it.

bank_turn_6.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_6.line: He leaves the vest on the basket. The green number on his rider chat has been blinking all week, and he has not answered it.

bank_turn_7.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_7.line: His pinky stays out. The novice's tripod is set, the phone is at three percent, and the family abroad is already awake.
bank_turn_7.bubble: Bank is waiting on a promise

bank_turn_8.speaker: char_bank
bank_turn_8.line: He says it without irony and without flattery. Then he picks up the vest and folds it small, the way he folds everything he owns.

finale.dialogue: The inverter hums. One phone drinks, then another. The funeral stream goes out at ten and the far time zones lean in.
Bank clips his phone to the last socket and stands guard over it like a man guarding a week with no hole in the turning.

obj_biscuit_tin.name: the biscuit tin of ledgers
obj_biscuit_tin.description: Biscuit tin, lid scratched from a decade of thumbs, three vendors' books inside sorted by who owes what and who has already paid.

obj_word_notebook.name: the word notebook
obj_word_notebook.description: Pocket notebook, cover soft from the pocket, pages of other people's words in Lek's small hand, none of them paid for.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Two small keys on a wire ring, one brass and one steel, worn smooth by the copy shop's stamp drawer opening and closing nine years.

obj_deed_bag.name: the deed in the rice bag
obj_deed_bag.description: Land deed folded into a rice bag, the bag washed and dried, the paper inside soft at the creases from being carried to offices that never quite registered it.

obj_coin_stack.name: the stack of ten-baht coins
obj_coin_stack.description: Ten-baht coins stacked in a column, counted twice, wrapped in a rubber band that has gone slack with use.

obj_permit_photo.name: the permit photo
obj_permit_photo.description: Passport-sized photo of a man in a collared shirt, the background blue, the corners bent from a plastic sleeve that has been opened too many times.

obj_laundry_basket.name: the laundry basket
obj_laundry_basket.description: Plastic basket, one handle cracked and taped, a green uniform folded on top and a phone charger coiled beside it.

obj_share_envelope.name: the circle envelope
obj_share_envelope.description: Brown envelope with a name penciled on the front and a payout inside, the flap folded twice and not sealed.

obj_vest_orange.name: the orange queue vest
obj_vest_orange.description: Orange delivery vest, reflective strip peeling at one shoulder, the green jacket underneath mended at the cuff with fishing line.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_bank
outcomeRules.line: Bank reads the ledgers upside down and finds the column where the soi's money has been standing still. 'This tin knows who owes who. That's a rotation I can trust.'

outcomeRules.speaker: char_bank
outcomeRules.line: He flips the notebook to the page where Lek has written the novice's name three ways and nods. 'You keep other people's words. Keep mine tonight: the stream first.'

outcomeRules.speaker: char_bank
outcomeRules.line: Bank takes the keys, opens the copy shop's stamp drawer, and counts out the coins the soi will pay for its charging hour. 'Cash that never slept. Here's your stack.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Received: the stack of ten-baht coins

char_bank: He turns the {item} over once and sets it back in Lek's hands. 'Not that. Not tonight.'
He looks at the {item}, then at the queue forming by the wat bell. 'The tin first. I need to know who owes what before I hand out hours.'
He taps the {item} against the step. 'Open the tin, clerk. Show me the books, and then we'll talk about the keys.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the dark with nothing settled. The inverter hums; the queue waits.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. Bank watches the charging corner the way a rider watches a red light.
Bank's gaze flicks from the {item} to the biscuit tin and back — a route mapped, a toll implied.
obj_deed_bag: The rice bag stays folded. Bank does not look at it. 'Land is a stillness I can't afford.'
He nudges the bag with his boot. 'That paper has been to every office on this soi and come back. It won't charge a phone.'
He picks up the bag, weighs it, and sets it down. 'If you want the keys, show me the tin first. The books, not the deed.'
obj_coin_stack: He counts the coins once and pushes them back. 'That's not the rotation I meant.'
He stacks the coins in a column and leaves them on the step. 'Cash that never slept, and still it doesn't move.'
He taps the coin stack. 'The tin first. Then the notebook. Then we'll talk about what the keys open.'
obj_permit_photo: He glances at the photo and looks away. 'A face in a sleeve won't hold a charge.'
He turns the photo face down on the step. 'That's a man waiting at a stop the bus no longer serves.'
He slides the photo back. 'The tin, clerk. Show me the books and I'll show you the keys.'
